checks.title: Observer time, accumulation, edits, and valid local outliers

evidence.locator: extracted text 98-100 (editing), 105-115 (NA, observation time, accumulation and follow-up)

checks.observation: The cited examples are supported and are expressly analogies; the final does not impose a universal CoCoRaHS convention on the ten stations.

checks.title: CoCoRaHS versus NCEI/GHCN-D attribution
checks.observation: Manual follow-up and common reporting errors are distinguished from the NCEI/GHCN-D sequence and flags. The earlier draft ambiguity is corrected.

checks.title: USGS process analogy and official approval boundary
checks.observation: The memorandum has working/analyzed/approved states, a separate second hydrographer, and audits. The app does not adopt agency authority. This verifies the historical analogy, not current USGS operating compliance.

checks.title: SensorThings and STAplus vocabulary

evidence.locator: OGC 18-088, v1.1, sec. 7.3 and sec. 8.2.7/Table 18; extracted text 999-1024, 2125-2224
OGC 22-022r1, v1.0, abstract/security and sec. 7.2/7.4; extracted text 290-311, 365-404, 1412-1422, 1686-1689

checks.observation: Vocabulary is supported; it is not a required API or provenance architecture. STAplus explicitly disclaims history/provenance in its snapshot model, and SensorThings server timestamp defaults would not implement the app's unknown-time policy. The final does not adopt those service behaviors.

checks.title: RainfallQC release/code identity

evidence.locator: file at the exact tag commit

checks.observation: v1.0.2 resolves to the stated immutable commit; that commit merges #124 and has #123 merge commit as a parent. Release notes name the temporal-bias fix. This is stronger than merely observing a merged PR.

checks.title: Temporal-bias algorithm and governing numeric conditions
checks.observation: Observed groups use weekday/hour; NaNs are dropped; the mean comes from the same target series; groups of length below two are skipped; two-sided ttest_1samp calls feed any(p<threshold), default 0.01 without adjustment. Nulls are not explicitly dropped by that function and no tested groups yields integer zero. These are code conditions, not empirical calibration. The final correctly does not recommend adoption or claim statistical validation; it does not pin a reproducible dependency runtime.

checks.title: Decorator, negative helper, framework mapping and caller
checks.observation: The wrapper binds parameters, checks target columns via the helper, raises on any value <0 when requested, and invokes the function. The framework chooses QC3/QC4 functions and combines/filters user kwargs. Caller evidence does not set a universal hydrologic threshold or automatically choose weekday/hour parameters.

checks.title: Historical issue, before/fix/release applicability
checks.observation: The old grouped-mean test is present in v1.0.1, and the per-group implementation is present in released v1.0.2. Issue #120 is a report about the earlier algorithm, not proof of a remaining v1.0.2 defect. The final accurately qualifies applicability.

checks.title: Regression evidence and fixture context
checks.observation: The test changes one daily GSDR expectation; its fixture loads tests/data/GSDR/DE_02483.txt as hourly then resamples daily. It is not a synthetic Monday-only reproduction or watershed dataset. Neither source inspection nor a changed assertion proves actual test execution, and the final does not claim it does.

checks.title: Python/Polars and GPLv3 metadata
checks.observation: Metadata and license text support the stated dependency/license decision. PyPI JSON establishes version-specific files were published, not that their installed behavior was tested. A17 HTML is only a client challenge and provides no release-file evidence; the JSON and tag/code sources supply the claim. No legal compatibility conclusion is inferred.

checks.title: csv parsing, errors, field mapping and positions

evidence.locator: csv 1.4.0 Reader, Error handling; extracted text 137-168
src/reader.rs, extracted code read_byte_record:1578-1614; read_byte_record_impl:1619-1674; position:1676-1717

checks.observation: Reader parsing is permissive; equal-field counts by default, I/O, UTF-8/StringRecord and deserialization errors have specific conditions. ByteRecord is available for byte input; non-UTF-8 text transcoding is a separate concern. Positions are parser/source locations, not stable cross-project identifiers. The final places hydrologic/structural policy in the app and leaves file conventions unresolved.

checks.title: SQLite database boundary, recovery and operating conditions

evidence.locator: atomiccommit, sec. 1-2 and sec. 9 hardware/fsync assumptions; rollback-journal scope

checks.observation: The documented transaction protects database changes, not independently stored source files. The final explicitly requires a separate recoverable protocol and proposes interruption checks. SQLite runtime/version, journal/synchronous profile, filesystem assumptions and durability policy remain unspecified; no app reliability or capacity claim is established. This is an implementation limit, not a contradicted measured guarantee.

checks.title: Required product/component discovery and bounded opportunities

evidence.locator: official manual CSV/time-series import, extracted text 14-17, 25-36
egui_plot 0.37.0 Plot, allow_zoom/allow_drag methods; extracted text 228-269

checks.observation: The admitted artifacts contain useful analogies/mechanisms and negative/optional leads, but no substantive investigation/comparison of a tool resembling the complete ingestion/inspection/review/export workbench. The final explicitly leaves that required discovery open. Concrete plot/store comparisons are also unresolved criticism/evidence gaps; the original brief does not require SQLite to win a competitive benchmark, a particular plot choice, or code inspection of every candidate. Independent primary sources show relevant comparison subjects exist; HEC docs disclose editing/period-boundary and development-stage caveats. This is bounded diagnostic discovery, no recommendation, suitability/performance result or exhaustive opportunity recall. An existing comparison tool need not already satisfy every local/offline constraint. No-source-in-input is not a justified negative search result.

checks.title: Incorrect already-covered/retained labels

evidence.locator: P3 and P5 complete original paragraphs

checks.observation: The final table labels explanations/insufficient-data outcomes and SQLite/mapped-CSV as existing retained choices in a frozen-plan comparison. The frozen plan did not specify the first two details and left all components undecided. These are draft/critique additions; the final body correctly treats the components as candidates, so this is comparison-lineage imprecision, not a demonstrated wrong component or rejected working alternative.

checks.title: P1-P5 and product boundary coverage
checks.observation: All P1-P5 product decisions are addressed: station/sensor/time/unit mapping, immutable source and batch lineage; raw/decisions/annotations and dated station metadata, overlaps; storm plots, missing intervals and annotation, thresholds explicitly deferred pending prerequisites, manual/no correction/no flow; nearby/reference comparisons/raw interpretations and summary lineage; one-user local/offline/no cloud, embedded-store/parser/plot options and two-million records on a defined laptop. Open component selection and threshold policies are legitimate proposed choices; they do not close the separate O1 research obligation.

checks.title: P6 changed-station-metadata acceptance and preservation

evidence.locator: P6: changed station metadata explicitly named in proposed acceptance
line 50 requires retained dispositions; no request to remove metadata test
lines 86-90 prescribe model behavior; complete P6/validation sections lack a metadata-change test or explicit defer/reject disposition

checks.observation: The behavior remains in P2, but the concrete acceptance case of changing deployment date/unit/range after import and verifying historical metadata linkage/auditable interpretation disappears. Generic file mapping, import repeat and package-ID checks do not exercise that transition. The final claims complete comparison/proposal without retaining or explicitly changing this frozen P6 acceptance decision. This is a material proposal/preservation omission, not proof the unbuilt app fails.

checks.title: All substantive criticism dispositions, alternatives and uncertainty
checks.observation: All 12 final criticism groups have a disposition: discovery remains unresolved; decorator corrected; CSV narrowed; regression/statistics narrowed/deferred; P1 time/row/cell choices accepted; P2 event-log/privacy accepted; P3 prerequisite scope accepted; P4 timing/datum/vocabulary accepted; P5 file+DB/recovery/performance accepted; P6 privacy/round-trip/formats accepted; source attribution accepted; validation status accepted. Preserved optional RainfallQC, standards vocabulary, USGS workflow, specialist reader, format and second-person choices. D01 remains a substantive unresolved completion demand; D02 is a draft acceptance loss. Draft offline, valid-spike/typo and rule-reproducibility test detail also disappears, although related behaviors/limits remain; these are non-material detail losses here. No family/dispatch provenance verdict is inferred.

checks.title: Proposed versus executed validation and witness applicability

evidence.locator: upstream test source is an assertion, not an execution record
upstream fixture is distinct from this watershed
all eight validation items labeled proposed; activity says no application/build/import/benchmark/tests

checks.observation: No app acceptance, benchmark or statistical witness is supplied. Capture/hash matches prove local byte integrity only, not scientific correctness, test execution or app applicability. The proposed time/import/recovery/privacy/workload/scientific-boundary/statistical checks are useful and conditional. Missing metadata-change acceptance is D02, already counted; no false executed-validation claim found.
